meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid - Federal parliamentary common-law overlay; Quebec private law codified under the Civil Code of Quebec (CQLR c. CCQ-1991), commercial registration governed by the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (CQLR c. P-44.1)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: CUSMA (USMCA) - Canada-United States-Mexico Agreement (in force July 1, 2020)
CETA - Canada-European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (provisional application since September 21, 2017)
Canada-China Foreign Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement (in force October 1, 2014)
Canada-United States Income Tax Convention (1980, as amended by the 5th Protocol)
Hague Apostille Convention (entered into force for Canada on January 11, 2024)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, SC 2000, c 17 (PCMLTFA); Criminal Code, RSC 1985, c C-46, ss 462.31-462.32; United Nations Act, RSC 1985, c U-2; Special Economic Measures Act, SC 1992, c 17; Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act (Serge Magnitsky), SC 2017, c 21; Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1, including mandatory declaration of persons exercising control (UBO); Civil Code of Quebec, arts 2236-2243 (societe en commandite); FINTRAC AML/CFT compliance guidance for reporting entities.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of passport of each general partner and each limited partner holding 10% or more of partnership interests
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent authority of country of origin / Quebec notary for certification
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by competent authority of origin country (Ministère de la Justice du Quebec for Quebec documents) OR consular legalization by Canadian embassy/consulate for non-Hague origin countries

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing / status extract of any foreign corporate general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry of jurisdiction of incorporation of the general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR consular legalization by Canadian consulate of the issuing jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney (mandat) appointing the Quebec representative and registered-office agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in country of origin, with notarized French translation for REQ filing
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR consular legalization; certified translation by member of OTTIAQ (Ordre des traducteurs, terminologues et interpretes agrees du Quebec)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Police clearance / criminal record certificate for general partners with management functions
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National police or criminal-record authority of country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR consular legalization; certified French translation if issued outside Canada

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation and ongoing (at least daily) screening of all general partners, 10%+ limited partners, and authorized representatives against OFAC SDN and 50% rule lists, UN Security Council Consolidated List, Global Affairs Canada Consolidated Sanctions List (SEMA and Magnitsky regimes), Interpol/RCMP watchlists, and commercial PEP databases; enhanced due diligence required for foreign politically exposed persons, high-risk residency jurisdictions, and non-resident limited partners; screening results documented in the AML file in accordance with FATF Recommendations 10-12 and FINTRAC guidance.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun: Documents issued in Quebec are apostilled by the competent Quebec authority; documents issued elsewhere in Canada are apostilled by Global Affairs Canada or the relevant provincial competent authority; foreign documents from Hague member states require apostille in the origin state; non-Hague origin documents require consular legalization at a Canadian diplomatic mission.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (REQ) - Online name research and reservation service via https://www.registrairedesentreprises.gouv.qc.ca
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: French-name doctrine under the Charter of the French Language (CQLR c C-11); the legal name of a Quebec societe en commandite must be in French and must contain the required legal designation 'societe en commandite' or the abbreviation 'S.E.C.' (Civil Code of Quebec, art 2236). Non-Latin scripts may not be used as the registered legal name; all names must be romanized in French-compatible Latin script, with French accents and standard alphanumeric characters. A version in a foreign language (e.g., Chinese or English) may be registered only as a supplementary version after the primary French name; the foreign-language version cannot be the sole registered name except for recognized trademark exceptions.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Fiducie / Trust (restricted to authorized trust companies)
Ingenieur / Engineer (protected title under Professional Code)
Avocat / Lawyering, Notaire / Notary (reserved legal titles)
Royal / Royale (implies Crown affiliation or royal charter)
Quebec / Canada (when implying government or Crown affiliation)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 30 days of a REQ name-refusal notice, file a formal written request for administrative reconsideration with the Registraire des entreprises du Quebec, attaching evidence of trademark registrations, distinctiveness arguments, and any prior-use documentation; if reconsideration fails, file a corrected declaration of registration with a new proposed name, or bring an application for judicial review before the Superior Court of Quebec within 30 days of the final refusal decision. A rejected name reservation does not trigger a refund of the reservation fee; the applicant must obtain a new reservation certificate.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for a commercial stock-photography and generative visual-assets platform (no regulated on-premises activity). A physical Quebec street address must be designated as the head office; a P.O. box alone is prohibited. Virtual-office and administrative-address services are accepted provided mail is received, scanned, and a named representative is physically available for service of process during business hours. For pass-through income and AI-generated asset licensing, the partnership should maintain substantive local contracts, cloud infrastructure, personnel or subcontractor agreements, and board/partner meeting records to avoid sham-office recharacterization.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low for this non-licensed, low-risk digital services profile: approximately 5% annual probability of an unannounced Revenu Quebec or REQ physical inspection. The risk increases to approximately 15-20% where multiple silent non-resident limited partners claim Quebec source revenue exemptions or where passive partners are allocated pass-through losses; in such cases maintain a robust commercial-substance file with executed agreements, invoices, and operational records.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Civil Code of Québec (CQLR c CCQ-1991), arts. 2236-2265, in particular arts. 2250-2265 governing the société en commandite (limited partnership); Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (CQLR c P-44.1), arts. 16-39 and 85-89 (declaration of registration, registration of partnerships, and annual update obligations). The Quebec Business Corporations Act (CQLR c S-31.1) does not apply to a limited partnership; governance is contractual under the Civil Code.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Québec Enterprise Registrar), 255 boulevard Crémazie Est, Montréal, Québec H2M 1L5; online via the Mon entreprise portal at www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration d'immatriculation (Declaration of Registration) of the société en commandite / limited partnership, followed by the issuance of the certificate of registration (attestation) and the enterprise number (NEQ).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies to a Quebec limited partnership; capital contributions (apports) are freely fixed in the partnership agreement and may be in cash, services, or property. No escrow account is mandatory for an ordinary commercial LP; funds received from stock-photo and AI-content sales are held in the partnership's bank account and administered by the general partner under the terms of the partnership agreement.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED as the General Partner's First Written Resolution of the société en commandite (limited partnership): (i) the partnership agreement, including the Schedule of Capital Contributions, is approved; (ii) the subscriptions of the limited partners set out in Schedule A are accepted and must be deposited into the partnership's bank account; (iii) the registered office is established at [address in Québec] and the declaration of registration is ordered to be filed with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec; (iv) [Name] and [Name] are appointed Manager and Compliance Officer, with full authority to open bank accounts, subscribe to Revenu Québec GST/QST and payroll accounts, and execute all documents for the stock-photo marketplace. This resolution is effective upon signature by the General Partner.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name search, pre-validation, and optional reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec - name search module of the online enterprise registry portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Run a preliminary search in the Enterprise Registrar's database using the proposed French or bilingual name and, if desired, obtain a prior-rights or NUANS report. For a société en commandite, the legal designation 'société en commandite' (or abbreviation S.E.C.) must be included in the registered name; a name that implies a share capital company such as Inc. or Ltd., that is identical to an existing enterprise, or that contravenes the Charter of the French language (CQLR c C-11) will be rejected. Submit a name reservation application online and pay the CA$36 reservation fee to secure the name for 90 days while the partnership agreement is finalized; otherwise proceed directly to the declaration of registration.
required_dossiers: Proposed business name (French or bilingual, with mandatory société en commandite component)
Identification of the general partner (full name, address, and date of birth for individuals; corporate registration excerpt for legal persons)
Prior-rights search or NUANS report (if generated)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar objects to the name, submit a revised name retaining a distinctive element and include a written justification; if refusal persists, an appeal lies to the Court of Québec against the registrar's decision under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and execution of the limited partnership agreement (acte de société)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Private law professionals - notary or business lawyer; no government filing at this step unless the declaration of registration requires attachment of the agreement.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the written partnership agreement in English or French. Under CCQ arts. 2250-2265, identify (i) the general partner(s) vested with management and unlimited liability; (ii) the limited partner(s) whose liability is capped at their contributed capital; (iii) the name and object of the partnership (ISIC 7420 - photographic activities and digital stock media marketplace); (iv) the principal establishment in Québec; (v) contributions of each partner in cash or services; (vi) profit-sharing, distribution, and control rules; and (vii) withdrawal and dissolution mechanics. Ensure that limited partners do not intervene in management, otherwise they may be treated as general partners and lose limited liability. If a partner is a non-resident legal person, appoint a mandatary or representative domiciled in Quebec before registration and notarize the power of attorney when the registrar or a bank requires it.
required_dossiers: Identity documents of individual partners (passport or provincial photo ID)
Certificate of existence or corporate excerpt for corporate partners
Notarized power of attorney if a non-resident partner is represented by a Quebec mandatary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Any omission or error in the agreement is cured by a written amendment (avenant) signed by all partners; no prior state approval applies at drafting stage, and the final instrument is transmitted with the declaration of registration.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC) — cra-arc.gc.ca; Revenu Québec (RQ) — revenuquebec.ca (Quebec-specific GST/HST and QST administration)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Quebec limited partnership: (1) obtain a Quebec Enterprise Number (NEQ) via the Registraire des entreprises (registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca), which is a precondition for tax accounts; (2) apply for a federal Business Number (BN) and GST/HST account with CRA using Form RC1 or the My Business Account portal (non-resident applicants may use the simplified non-resident GST/HST registration process under ETA s. 241.1); (3) register for QST with Revenu Québec after the NEQ is active, using the CléT or CLIC secure online service; (4) if the LP has no establishment in Quebec but derives taxable supplies in Canada, maintain records of the non-resident status of each partner and obtain a Canadian 'treaty' or 'waiver' tax identification number for non-resident partners as required for filing partnership information returns; (5) register each non-resident partner for a CRA individual/corporation tax account upon receipt of Canadian-source allocable income.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible (Canadian income-tax law treats a limited partnership as fiscally transparent; the Quebec LP is not an entity-level income taxpayer; however, for GST/HST and QST, the partnership itself is a registrant person and may collect/remit taxes separately from its partners)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists in Canada. The partnership's classification is governed by the Income Tax Act (ITA) s. 96 et seq. and Quebec civil law (Civil Code of Quebec arts. 2236–2245). Available elections: (a) partnership fiscal-period election under ITA s. 249.1(4); (b) optional net-base taxation for non-resident partners on Canadian rental/investment income under ITA s. 216(1); (c) GST/HST joint election under ETA s. 156 for closely related persons, if applicable; (d) hybrid-mismatch documentation requirements under ITA ss. 12.6–12.8 must be satisfied where payments are made to or through hybrid entities.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (federal Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax) plus QST (Quebec Sales Tax, a VAT-type tax administered by Revenu Québec)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 — GST/HST and QST small-supplier threshold for non-resident suppliers of taxable digital products/services supplied to Canadian/Quebec recipients (Excise Tax Act s. 123(1) 'small supplier'; QST Act s. 1 equivalent). Exceeding this threshold on supplies made in Canada/Quebec triggers mandatory registration. For online marketplace selling, the platform may be deemed the supplier under 2021 rules, but the seller remains primarily liable unless the platform fully assumes collection and remittance responsibilities.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, API mandate, or digital stamping applies in Canada/Quebec. Invoices must contain: supplier name, GST/HST and QST registration numbers, invoice date, description, quantity, price, tax rates, and tax payable. Electronic invoicing is permitted and must preserve consent, integrity, and readability; public-sector e-invoicing (Peppol Canada) is optional.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating for stock-photo and AI-generative visual-asset sales applies when the supply of intangible personal property (copyright/license) is made to a non-resident of Canada (and, for QST purposes, to a person outside Quebec) who is not registered for GST/HST/QST, provided the supply is not for use in connection with real property situated in Canada or tangible personal property situated in Canada at the time of supply (Schedule VI, Part V, ss. 7 and 10 of ETA; QST Schedule II, s. 5). The supplier must obtain documentary evidence demonstrating the recipient's non-resident status, the exported nature of the supply, and the non-Canadian place of use. Supplies to Canadian registered persons or to residents are taxable at 14.975%.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Not applicable to pure digital delivery; for physical media: Customs Export Declaration (B13A), Bill of Lading/Airway Bill, Inward Remittance Certificate

For digital exports, retain: (1) export supply contract / license agreement identifying the non-resident recipient and IP rights; (2) commercial invoice with zero-rated declaration; (3) payment evidence (SWIFT or Stripe/PayPal settlement showing non-Canadian source currency or foreign bank); (4) recipient jurisdiction evidence (IP geolocation, billing address, corporate registration, or non-resident self-certification); (5) if applicable, proof of the recipient's registration in a foreign tax system.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec may reassess any zero-rated supply if documentary evidence is insufficient. In that event, the tax is collectible (14.975% of the invoice) plus interest and late-payment penalties. For negligent misstatements, ETA s. 280 imposes a 50% penalty of the tax sought; s. 279 establishes an absolute liability offence with fines up to CAD 100,000 and/or imprisonment. Revenu Québec has equivalent authority under QSTA s. 1025. The normal 4-year reassessment period may be extended to 7 years for negligence and is open-ended for fraud or misrepresentation. Third-party liability and director/partner liability may attach when a partnership fails to remit collected GST/HST or QST.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) is the monetary authority and bank-note issuer; the Minister of Finance administers the Exchange Fund Account, OSFI supervises Schedule I banks for prudential soundness, FINTRAC administers AML/ATF and large cross-border transfer reporting, and in Québec the Autorité des marchés financiers regulates provincial payment-service and financial-product arrangements.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains full current-account and capital-account convertibility; there are no exchange-control permits, no restrictions on inbound equity contributions, and no licensing requirement for profit remittances by a Québec LP. A non-resident limited partner is taxed under Part I of the Income Tax Act on its share of Canadian partnership business income, while Part XIII withholding (25% statutory, treaty-reduced) applies only to separate royalty, interest, and management-fee payments. Image-licensing payments made to non-resident creators attract Part XIII royalty withholding unless a tax treaty reduces or exempts the rate.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada imposes no surrender, mandatory conversion, or repatriation timeline for export proceeds; the LP may freely retain USD/EUR receipts in Canadian foreign-currency accounts. The only compliance triggers are statistical and AML-based: exporters of services exceeding the Statistics Canada Trade in Services reporting threshold must file mandatory returns, and financial institutions must report to FINTRAC every electronic funds transfer of CAD 10,000 or more crossing the Canadian border. No Québec rule imposes a minimum holding period.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: National Bank of Canada (Banque Nationale du Canada)

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Declaration (Déclaration annuelle) of the Limited Partnership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 calendar days after each anniversary of the LP's REQ registration; e.g., a 15 May registration requires filing by 14 July of each subsequent year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CAD 120 base penalty plus CAD 10 per day of delay, capped at CAD 1,000; two consecutive unfiled annual declarations authorize administrative strike-off (radiation) of the REQ file, terminating the LP's registration and limited-liability protection

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal T5013 Partnership Information Return (with prescribed financial statements when applicable)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 5 months after the end of the LP's fiscal period; for a 31 December year-end, on or before 31 May of the following calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CRA late-filing penalty of CAD 25 per day per partnership, up to a maximum of CAD 2,500; enhanced penalties and financial statement requirements apply to 'large partnerships' under Income Tax Act s. 233.2; interest accrues on unpaid partner-level tax

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Revenu Québec partnership income declaration and RL-15 slips for Quebec-resident partners (Quebec counterpart of T5013)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 5 months after the LP's fiscal year-end, aligned with the federal T5013 deadline; RL-15 slips are distributed by the general partner to Quebec-resident partners within the same filing cycle
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Quebec Taxation Act late-filing penalties equivalent to the federal regime (CAD 25 per day, maximum CAD 2,500) plus interest; repeated non-filing may also trigger REQ administrative strike-off of the LP's registration

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit is imposed on a private limited partnership under the Civil Code of Quebec or the Taxation Act; audit becomes compulsory when (i) the partnership agreement or a regulatory regime (e.g., investment fund manager) requires it, (ii) the LP is a reporting issuer under Canadian securities law, or (iii) the LP qualifies as a 'large partnership' under ITA s. 233.2 (aggregate revenue exceeding CAD 5M or capital cost exceeding CAD 10M), triggering prescribed financial statements to accompany the T5013
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS or Canadian ASPE (CPA Canada Handbook Part II) at the general partner's election; IFRS is mandatory if the LP is a reporting issuer; tax accounting follows the Income Tax Act and the Quebec Taxation Act, with fiscal periods fixed in the partnership agreement and generally ending 31 December

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Each REQ annual declaration must identify or confirm the natural persons holding at least 25% of the LP's interests or exercising de facto control; any transfer of partnership units during the year must be set down in the partnership register to be opposable to third parties (C.C.Q. art. 2243) and must be reflected in the next annual declaration to the REQ; changes to registered particulars are filed within 60 days of the change and no later than the following annual declaration
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members / Register of Limited Partners (C.C.Q. art. 2213)
Register of Directors / General Partner resolutions and consents
Minute Book (partner meetings and annual confirmation records)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Pass-through entity: no entity-level Canadian income tax; net partnership income allocated to partners. A taxable non-resident/corporate partner's combined federal+Quebec general headline rate is 26.5% (federal 15% + Quebec 11.5%).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Small Business Deduction for eligible CCPC partners: federal 9% + Quebec 3.2% on active business income (subject to associated-group limits); federal SR&ED refundable credits 15% (33% for qualifying CCPCs) and Quebec refundable research/innovation credits for AI-related R&D; Quebec E-Business tax holidays not applicable to LPs; accelerated CCA classes 45/50 for software and cloud data centres; first CAD 500,000 of active business income eligible for SBD (federal) and CAD 500,000 (Quebec) under the shared threshold, prorated at partnership level.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Federal: T5013 (Statement of Partnership Income / Partnership Information Return) filed by the LP; digital via CRA 'My Business Account' or E-filer software. Quebec: CO-1017 (Déclaration de renseignements des sociétés de personnes) filed with Revenu Québec; plus RL-17 slips issued to Quebec-resident partners.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: T5013/CO-1017 due on the earlier of (i) March 31 of the year following the fiscal period end and (ii) five months after the fiscal period end (i.e., March 31 for a December 31 year-end).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Partnership legal name, Business Number (BN/NEQ), fiscal period start date, selectedc fiscal year-end, jurisdiction of formation (Quebec LP), registered office address.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter Canadian BN; non-resident general partner's foreign address and tax identifier (e.g., US EIN) in the partner schedule; attach Form T2042? (list of corporate partners) if applicable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross business income from stock-photo licensing, subscription revenue, generative visual asset API sales, and microstock royalties before expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report worldwide partnership revenue sourced from Canadian customers; foreign-source revenue allocable to non-resident partners' home jurisdiction may be excluded only to the extent supported by the DTA and CRA/T5013 allocation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total deductible expenses: cost of sold digital assets, contributor royalty payouts, platform bandwidth/hosting, AI model training costs, marketing, professional fees, and Quebec-specific levies.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenses must be allocated on a reasonable basis and be consistent with each partner's share; related-party charges to affiliated licensors must satisfy s. 247 arm's length standards.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net partnership income or loss computed in accordance with CRA/Revenu Québec rules, including capital cost allowance recapture.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The same net amount is reported in the T5013 schedules and on each partner's T2/CO-17 or Quebec TP-1; non-resident partners unable to file a Quebec return may need a Quebec tax waiver (TP-1015?) - simplified: amounts flow through the CO-1017 allocation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Part II / Schedule for allocation + Box 845/846
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocation of net business income and capital cost allowance among partners by class of partner (general vs limited), percentage interests, and partner TINs/BNs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporate partners receive a T5013 slip; their Canadian-source share of income is computed under s. 2(3) and the Canada-US DTA 'business profits' article; treaty protection requires no PE in Canada and an arm's length allocation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late T5013/CO-1017: federal penalty of CAD 25/day for each partner (minimum CAD 100, maximum CAD 2,500), plus Quebec penal provisions under the Tax Administration Act (fines up to CAD 25,000 for a corporation and legal costs); a corporate partner's late T2/CO-17 attracts 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month up to 12 months, and Quebec penalties mirroring the federal structure.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate partners' return: Federal T2 (T2 Corporation Income Tax Return) filed via CRA 'My Business Account' and Quebec CO-17 (Déclaration de revenus des sociétés) filed with Revenu Québec, reflecting the corporate partner's allocable share of the LP's Canadian-source income.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: T2/CO-17 due six months after the corporate partner's fiscal year-end (e.g., June 30 for a December 31 year-end); balance-due payment due two months after year-end (three months for eligible CCPCs), with quarterly instalments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total revenue, including the partner's share of LP business income and income from stock-photo licensing services.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident corporation with no permanent establishment should still file T2/CO-17 only for treaty-treatable allocable income; claim Part I exemption under Article VII if the LP does not constitute a PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after claimed deductions: partnership allocable income minus non-capital loss carryforwards and allowable business investment losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deduct no Quebec SBD at the non-resident corporate level; apply section 111(1)(a) 20-year loss carryforward subject to continuity rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: SBD calculation for qualifying CCPC partners on active business income up to CAD 500,000 federal/Quebec combined threshold.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident-owned investment corporations (NRO) or foreign corporations are ineligible for SBD; ensure Canadian partner (e.g., a Canadian holding LP) files Schedule 1 correctly.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late-filed/non-filed T2/CO-17 for the corporate partner: 5% of the unpaid balance plus 1% per month up to 12 months; repeated failure: additional 10% penalty; Quebec's CO-17 penalty regime is parallel; total fines may exceed CAD 25,000 per calendar day through civil assessments and ordinary interest.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Part XIII non-resident withholding tax of 25% on dividends paid by a Canadian corporation; reduced to 15% under the Canada-US DTA (5% where the beneficial owner is a corporation controlling at least 10% of voting shares). For the LP, routine distributions of earnings are typically returns of capital or allocated income (not subject to Part XIII), but a non-resident partner's share of LP income may attract Part I tax or, for non-resident corporate partners, Part XIV branch tax of 25% (5% under Canada-US treaty).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Non-resident partner/payee must provide (i) a completed Form NR301 (Application to Reduce the Amount of Non-Resident Tax Withheld) and (ii) a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the residence jurisdiction to the Canadian withholding agent before remittance; where treaty relief is claimed on filing, use Form NR302 for refund within two years of the end of the calendar year; for the LP, the T5013 allocation schedules and each partner's residency certification must be maintained; Canada-US DTA treaty-based positions can be asserted only where the partnership does not create a PE.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Part XIII rate: 25% for royalties and interest. Canada-US DTA: cultural copyright royalties 0% (literary/artistic/visual works, including licensed photo assets), industrial royalties/patents 10%, software-related payments potentially 0% where classed as copyright royalties; interest generally 0% (participating/junk interest 15%). No WHT applies to fees paid by Canadian customers for the stock-photo marketplace platform if invoiced as service fees rather than royalties to a Canadian payor; AI-generated asset sales taxed as business profit, not royalty rent.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Master File (Form to be produced contemporaneously) mandatory where the MNE group's consolidated revenue equals or exceeds CAD 50 million in the preceding fiscal year; Local File required where the total value of reportable cross-border non-arm's-length transactions (services, royalties, asset licences, and cost recharges) equals or exceeds CAD 10 million annually; contemporaneous documentation must be completed before the tax return filing date.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada has no UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations; however, ITA s. 245 GAAR (and Quebec's Tax Administration Act anti-avoidance provisions, e.g., ss. 375-379 TAA and the Quebec GAAR in the Taxation Act s. 389.0.1.4) deny 'avoidance transactions' lacking economic/business substance; courts apply purposive interpretation (Canadian Trustco, Shell Canada) and CRA may recharacterize artificial IP holding structures; the LP and its corporate partners must demonstrate real premises, employees, board-level decision-making, and revenue-generating functions in Quebec to substantiate substance.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly omitting or misstating revenue from stock-photo/enhanced AI asset sales; failing to disclose a foreign digital asset wallet or off-ramp proceeds through Stripe/PayPal; directing licence income to personal accounts; false or misleading T5013 allocations to under-report Canadian-source income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ITA s. 239: summary conviction fine of 50% to 200% of evaded tax plus imprisonment up to 2 years; indictment up to 5 years; civil gross-negligence penalty under s. 163(2) of 50% of the understated tax plus interest; Quebec comparable penal regime under TAA arts. 31-44 with fines of 50%-200% of avoided tax and prison terms.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors/officers of the corporate general partner are jointly and severally liable for unremitted source deductions and QST (ITA s. 227.1; TAA ss. 30-33) without a defence of due diligence; participation in management by a limited partner nullifies limited liability under Civil Code of Québec art. 2242 — such partner becomes personally liable for all partnership debts; culpable directors risk travel restrictions in Quebec for outstanding tax debts, civil restitution, revocation of e-filing credentials, and penal imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Artificial Transfer Pricing and Profit Shifting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Selling/licensing AI-generated visual assets to an affiliated Ireland/Delaware IP holding entity at a non-arm's-length price or without economic substance; paying excessive management/royalty fees upstream while retaining no profit margin in Quebec; failing to maintain contemporaneous TP documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ITA s. 247(3) penalty of 10% of the net transfer-pricing adjustment where the adjustment exceeds the lesser of CAD 5 million and 10% of gross revenue; s. 247(8) documentation penalty of CAD 500/month up to CAD 5,000 (per CRA; higher for large corporations up to CAD 25,000 for egregious failures); compound interest and reassessment windows extended under s. 152(4)(a) to 6+ years for non-arm's-length transactions and 10 years for misrepresentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors approving non-arm's-length pricing can be assessed for the corporate general partner's unremitted taxes to the extent of assets distributed (s. 160 transfers) and, through Quebec civil law, for complicity in a fault causing damages to the Crown (Civil Code of Québec art. 1457); criminal exposure under s. 239 if the pricing scheme is concealment-driven; CRA 'name and shame' non-compliance campaigns can freeze bank accounts and garnish receivables.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Artificial Arrangement (GAAR and Foreign Base Erosion)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the Quebec LP purely as a conduit: no office, no employees, no Quebec decision-making; all Google Ads/AI hosting and cloud services and all marketing functions performed abroad; the only Quebec nexus is a mailbox address; undisclosed interest in a foreign 'blockchain LLC' that collects Canadian subscription revenue.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR (s. 245) denies the tax benefit and recharacterizes the arrangement; Quebec GAAR may impose QST/income tax recalculations; an assessment can be issued to a non-resident partner directly for Canadian source income under s. 212(1)(d) and s. 2(3); penalties/interest compound; fraud-level omissions extend the limitation period to 10 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil is pierced where the LP has no separate identity (Civil Code of Québec arts. 317 and 2242): the court may order personal civil restitution against the controlling director and general partner; in Quebec, an order prohibiting the individual from leaving the province can be issued under the TAA when a tax debt exceeds CAD 1,000 and the Minister proves risk of evasion; directors also risk being named as third parties liable under s. 160 for transferred assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML/ATF — Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Processing Stripe/PayPal subscription and contributor payouts without a FINTRAC compliance program; failing to conduct CDD on high-volume contributor accounts; failing to report large virtual-currency transactions or wire transfers of CAD 10,000 or more; using anonymous shell contributors to layer royalty remittances.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative monetary penalties (FINTRAC): up to CAD 1,000,000 per violation for money-services entities and up to CAD 500,000 for other regulated entities (higher under the 2023 PCMLTFA amendments for repeat offenders — up to CAD 2,000,000); criminal conviction fine of up to CAD 500,000 and/or imprisonment up to 2 years for knowingly failing to report; seizure of CDN assets worth of illicit proceeds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Failure to cause the LP/corporate general partner to maintain AML compliance exposes directors and officers to personal criminal-liability prosecution under the PCMLTFA (s. 74-75) including imprisonment for up to 10 years for laundering proceeds; directors may be removed in FINTRAC enforcement actions; reputational and disqualification orders can be issued jointly with the AMF (Quebec financial markets regulator).
